svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.20.11.2 Bonding and Tying Intersecting Masonry Walls where Walls Require Lateral Support
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.20 MASONRY AND INSULATING CONCRETE FORM WALLS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND
Bonding and Tying Intersecting Masonry Walls where Walls Require Lateral Support

g.text: Unit of the intersecting wall embedded in
Corrosion-resistant metal tie, not less than
Ties not more than 800 mm apart vertically,
Both ends shaped to give a mechanical key
that develops the strength of the tie, (3)(d)
Every second course bonded: 50% of the
adjacent units, uniform over the height

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Where required to provide lateral support,
intersecting walls are bonded or tied
together.
Where bonding is used, 50% of the adjacent
masonry units in the intersecting wall,
distributed uniformly over the height of the
intersection, are embedded in the laterally
supported wall.
Where tying is used, the ties are
(a) corrosion-resistant metal, (b) equivalent to
not less than 4.76 mm by 40 mm steel strapping,
(c) spaced not more than 800 mm (31½″) o.c.
vertically, and (d) shaped at both ends to
provide sufficient mechanical key to develop the
strength of the ties.
Drawn: units without cores. A two courses lifted apart, embedded units tinted pink. B ties red, dashed where in the wall, top tie shown with the course above removed.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.20.11.2. (page 9-148)
